newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee steady at 35.70 v dlr after RBI moves.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee steady at 35.70 v dlr after RBI moves.

text.p: The Indian rupee was steady at 35.70 in mid-morning trade after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) made a surprise intervention early on Monday, dealers said.
Foreign banks - especially those who usually sell on behalf of foreign institutional investors (FIIs) in Indian stock markets -- were selling dollar heavily, they said.
"The dollar is now at 35.7000/7050 rupees," a dealer said.
The rupee was trading at 35.6950/6925 until RBI arrived on the scene.
Accumulated inward remittances over a long weekend added to the oversupply of dollars on Monday, dealers said. Friday was a holiday for banks in Bombay.
According to the latest data released by the Bombay Stock Exchange, net FII purchases on the bourse amounted to 350 million rupees on July 16.
The market opened below 35.70 in the expectation that the RBI would enter the market only in the closing hour, as was its practice last week, dealers said.
"Last few months' INR (Indian rupee) movement has hardened market sentiment that dollar has to be sold on every RBI-sponsored rally," Societe Generale said in a commentary.
"Is regular RBI intervention falling into a diminishing marginal return syndrome?" it asked.
